g.text: RPF failure — the packet arrived on an interface that is not the route back to the source

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
# Reverse-path-forwarding check — a small figure that reads RIGHT TO LEFT. # # What this figure probes: four constructs that had no demonstrator anywhere in # the corpus before this release. They are gathered into one small document on # purpose — a capability needs A demonstrator, not a document of its own. # # 1. `flow left` — the reverse direction. Twelve figures in this corpus use # `flow right` and twelve use `flow down`; `left` and `up` # had none, so half of the enum was untested by any figure. # 2. `\"` escape — a literal double quote INSIDE a quoted label. # 3. `#` inside a — a `[...]` region is verbatim (`VERBATIM-REGION-SCOPE`): the # bracketed comment mark loses its meaning inside one, so an edge # edge label label may carry a `#` without quoting or escaping it. # 4. a NEGATIVE — `at=` is canvas px and the origin is not a wall. A pin may # `at=` pin sit at a negative coordinate; the engine translates the # whole scene so the canvas still starts at (0,0). # # The subject fits the direction: an RPF check runs BACKWARDS along the path a # packet arrived on, so a figure that reads right to left is the honest layout, # not a stunt. That is the test for `flow left` in real use — if reversing the # reading order does not say something about the subject, use `flow right`. figdown 0.1 block title "RPF check on a multicast join"
class fail "RPF failure — the packet arrived on an interface that is not the route back to the source" stroke=#b91c1c style=dashed
# The source is on the RIGHT because the check walks back TOWARDS it. external src "from 198.51.100.7" # `\n` (a line break) and `\\` (a literal backslash) are the other two escapes # the grammar defines — core §11 lists exactly three, and all three are in this # file. The interface filter is a regex, which is where a backslash occurs # naturally in a network figure rather than as a demonstration of itself. node rx "Ingress ge-0/0/1\nfilter ge-0/0/\\d+" shape=rounded node lookup "Unicast RIB lookup" shape=box # The escape `\"` puts a literal double quote inside a quoted label. The label # is one token to the parser either way — the quotes delimit it, the backslash # says "this quote is data". node verdict "Arrived on the \"upstream\" interface?" shape=diamond node accept "Accept and forward" shape=rounded node drop "Drop (RPF fail)" shape=rounded class=fail
# `#` inside a bracketed edge label. Before `VERBATIM-REGION-SCOPE` this needed quoting, because # the comment scanner ran before the label scanner and ate the rest of the line; # the ruling made a verbatim region protect EVERY mark, not just the one that # earned the rule. So `[VRF #7]` is four characters of label, not a comment. edge src -[VRF #7]-> rx edge rx -> lookup edge lookup -[next-hop ge-0/0/1]-> verdict edge verdict -[yes]-> accept edge verdict -[no]-> drop class=fail
# `left` is the whole point of this document: the scene's flow axis runs from # the source on the right back to the verdict on the left. One `flow` line per # document (a second is a line error) — direction is a property of the figure. flow left rank accept,drop
# Layout zone: geometry only, no meaning. Strip it and the figure still says # the same thing (`GUI-WRITEBACK-STRUCTURE`). layout # A negative coordinate. `at=` is canvas px, and the canvas origin is a # reference point, not a wall: this nudge places the two verdict outcomes # above the main axis, and the engine shifts the whole scene so the rendered # canvas still begins at (0,0). Nothing is clipped and no other pin has to be # rewritten to compensate. pin drop at=(-30,0)
